cards.name: Write Technical Requirement Document (TRD)
cards.desc: Create a comprehensive TRD covering the Time-Off Microservice architecture, API design, data model, HCM integration strategy, sync mechanisms, and error handling. Must include challenges, proposed solutions, and alternatives considered.
checklist: Define system architecture and module boundaries
Design REST API contract (endpoints, DTOs, error responses)
Design data model (employees, balances, requests, sync log)
Document HCM real-time and batch integration strategy
Document conflict resolution and defensive validation approach
List challenges and alternatives considered
Peer review and finalize

cards.name: Setup SQLite + TypeORM infrastructure
cards.desc: Add TypeORM with SQLite driver to the NestJS project. Configure database module, migrations setup, and base entity patterns. This unblocks all feature modules.
checklist: Install @nestjs/typeorm, typeorm, better-sqlite3
Create DatabaseModule with SQLite configuration
Configure test database (in-memory SQLite for tests)
Verify module loads and connection works

cards.name: Employee balance module — entities & CRUD
cards.desc: Core module to track time-off balances per employee per location. This is the foundation the request and sync modules depend on. Balances represent the local mirror of HCM data.
checklist: Create Balance entity (employeeId, locationId, policyType, available, used, pending)
Create BalanceModule with service and controller
GET /balances/:employeeId — list balances for an employee
GET /balances/:employeeId/:locationId — balance for specific location
Write unit tests for BalanceService
Write e2e tests for balance endpoints

cards.name: Time-off request module — lifecycle management
cards.desc: Module to handle the full lifecycle of a time-off request: create, approve, reject, cancel. Must validate against local balance and later against HCM. Depends on balance module.
checklist: Create TimeOffRequest entity (employeeId, locationId, type, startDate, endDate, days, status)
Create RequestModule with service and controller
POST /requests — create a new time-off request (status: PENDING)
PATCH /requests/:id/approve — manager approval (status: APPROVED)
PATCH /requests/:id/reject — manager rejection (status: REJECTED)
PATCH /requests/:id/cancel — employee cancellation (status: CANCELLED)
Validate balance sufficiency on request creation
Track pending days in balance (optimistic hold)
Write unit tests for RequestService
Write e2e tests for request lifecycle endpoints

cards.name: HCM integration — real-time API client
cards.desc: Client module to communicate with the HCM real-time API for getting and sending time-off values. Used during request approval to validate with HCM and submit approved requests.
checklist: Create HcmModule with HcmClientService
Implement getBalance(employeeId, locationId) — fetch from HCM
Implement submitTimeOff(employeeId, locationId, days) — send to HCM
Handle HCM error responses (invalid dimensions, insufficient balance)
Implement retry logic with exponential backoff
Write unit tests with mocked HCM responses

cards.name: HCM integration — batch sync endpoint
cards.desc: Endpoint to receive bulk balance data from HCM. HCM can push the entire corpus of balances to ExampleHR. Must reconcile incoming data with local state and flag conflicts.
checklist: POST /sync/batch — receive bulk balance payload from HCM
Upsert balances from batch data
Detect and log conflicts (local pending requests vs updated balances)
Create SyncLog entity to track sync history
Write unit tests for batch reconciliation logic
Write e2e tests for batch sync endpoint

cards.name: Defensive validation layer
cards.desc: HCM validation is not always guaranteed. Implement a local defensive validation layer that checks balance sufficiency, dimension validity, and request consistency before and independently of HCM.
checklist: Local balance sufficiency check (available - pending >= requested)
Date range validation (no overlaps, no past dates, max duration)
Dimension validation (valid locationId for employeeId)
Double-submission guard (idempotency on request creation)
Write unit tests for each validation rule

cards.name: Mock HCM server for testing
cards.desc: Build a mock HCM server that simulates real-time and batch endpoints with configurable behavior — success, errors, balance changes, latency. Essential for integration tests and proving system robustness.
checklist: Create standalone mock HCM NestJS app or express server
Mock GET balance endpoint with configurable responses
Mock POST submit time-off with success/error scenarios
Mock batch endpoint that sends full balance corpus
Simulate external balance changes (anniversary bonus, yearly reset)
Simulate error scenarios (invalid dimensions, server down, timeout)
Make mock configurable per-test scenario

cards.name: Integration test suite
cards.desc: End-to-end integration tests that exercise the full request lifecycle with the mock HCM server. Must cover happy paths, conflict scenarios, and error resilience.
checklist: Test: full request lifecycle (create -> approve -> HCM submit -> balance update)
Test: request rejected by HCM insufficient balance
Test: batch sync updates local balances correctly
Test: batch sync detects conflict with pending requests
Test: HCM unavailable — defensive validation still works
Test: concurrent requests don't overdraw balance
Test: balance refresh (anniversary/yearly) reconciles correctly
Generate and verify coverage report

cards.name: Error handling & exception filters
cards.desc: Implement NestJS exception filters for consistent API error responses. Map HCM errors, validation errors, and internal errors to proper HTTP responses with clear messages.
checklist: Create global exception filter
Map HCM client errors to appropriate HTTP status codes
Standardize error response format (code, message, details)
Write tests for error response format

cards.name: API documentation with Swagger
cards.desc: Add Swagger/OpenAPI documentation to all endpoints so the API is self-documenting and easy to explore.
checklist: Install @nestjs/swagger
Add decorators to all DTOs and controllers
Configure Swagger UI at /api/docs
Verify all endpoints documented correctly
